description: The MCP tools Uncut gives the agent (Claude Code, Codex, ACP agents). Modules add their own agentTools (e.g. argent_record) on top. Every edit goes through timeline_edit, so it is checked, undoable per turn and attributed.

tools.name: project_read
tools.description: Read the project and its revision (pass it as timeline_edit's baseRevision). 'summary' (default) gives the canvas, media, tracks with their mixer and items, the master and notes; a long project's items come as compact lines (id, type, start, duration, media, text) unless you pass range or items. 'items' gives every field of every item (or of the ids in items): read an item this way before update_item, which replaces style, transform and effects whole. 'full' gives project.json.

items.description: Only these items, with every field.

tools.returns: revision, duration, and the project summary or full JSON

tools.name: timeline_edit
tools.description:
Apply edit ops atomically: one call is one undo step in your turn. Pass the revision you last read as baseRevision; if the user changed the same items since then, the edit is refused and you get their changes. A refusal gives each problem a fix (a start frame, a track, a free id): use it as it is. dryRun: true returns the planned lines, diff and conflicts without applying.
Edit ops (fields in the schema): insert_item (main track: index, default the end; other tracks: the item needs a start), update_item (null removes a field; transform, style, animation, effects and keys are replaced whole, so send what you keep), trim_item (frames > 0 shortens, < 0 lengthens; on main the rest ripples), split_item (at counts from the item's start; the second half gets newId), move_item (main: index; other tracks: start), delete_item (on main the rest closes up), set_transition (on the incoming main item, not the first; null clears it; modules_list kind "transition" lists the modules and their frame limits; allowTrim: true trims the spare media an overlap lacks), add_track, update_track (mixer replaced whole), delete_track, add_media, update_media, delete_media (no item may still use it), update_project (master replaced whole).
docs_read edits gives every op's fields and rules; docs_read text, picture and sound give the style, transform, keys, effects and mixer fields.

summary.description: One line the user sees in the turn card, e.g. 'Cut the shaky parts of the ridge shot'.

dryRun.description: Check the edit and return what it would do (planned ops, lines, diff, new length) or its conflicts with fixes; nothing changes.

tools.returns: { ok, revision, duration, seconds, placed? (where place_item or allowTrim put things), userChanges? }, or a refusal: { refused, details (each problem, with a fix), fix?, shapes? (the shape of each op it names), revision, userChanges? }; with dryRun: { lines (one per planned op), diff (added, removed, moved), duration } and nothing changes

tools.name: render_frames
tools.description: Render frames of the edit exactly as export would, as images (768 px on the longest side; scale 1 for full size). Up to 12 per call: pick the moments that matter. For motion use run: up to 48 frames in a row as one sheet, measured at full size for 1 px text shake and edge lines that stills miss.

phone.description: Draw them 360 px wide, the size of a phone in a feed, to judge readability (overrides scale).

run.description: Instead of frames: count frames in a row from start.

tools.returns: one image per frame, or one contact sheet and the motion measured for a run

tools.name: contact_sheet
tools.description: One image with a grid of frames, each captioned with its frame and time: from a media file (pulled from the original) or from the edit (drawn as the export draws it). Cheaper than many render_frames for scanning footage. 'every' samples every N frames; without it, 'max' frames (default 24) are spread evenly. 'at: shots' (with media) shows one frame per shot (the middle of each), from the video analysis (run now if needed, cached after). At most 60 cells.

media.description: A media id from project_read. Frames and range are then in project frames of that media (like an item's in).

range.description: Frames [start, end): of the edit, or of the media when media is given. Default: all of it.

every.description: Frames between samples when at is 'every'.

max.description: Most cells (default 24 when every isn't given).

tools.returns: one JPEG (at most 1600 px wide) and, as text, the frame and time of every cell in order (with at: shots, each shot's frames too); at: shots while the analysis still runs: { video: { state: running | queued }, note } (call again)

tools.name: media_analyze
tools.description: Analyse a media file. 'loudness' (also 'silence'): integrated loudness (LUFS), loudness range, true peak and the silences (below -40 dB for at least 0.3 s). 'video' (also 'shots', 'motion', 'stability'): cuts, frozen stretches and, per second, stability (no camera shake), sharpness, exposure and a cleanScore 0-1, with the best stretch inside one shot. Frames in the answer are usable as in. Waits up to a minute; if it answers running, call again. Cached by content. 'transcript': the speech transcribed on this Mac (a summary: language, word, filler and pause counts; transcript_read gives the words). 'beats' (also 'rhythm', 'onsets', 'tempo'): tempo (bpm), a confidence 0-1 and the beats in project frames of the media (the first ones, or those in range with the onsets there).

analyzers.description: Which analyses (default: loudness with silences; name video or beats to get them; video takes longer). silence = loudness; shots, motion, stability = video; rhythm, onsets, tempo = beats.

range.description: Only list what overlaps these project frames of the media [start, end); the whole file is always measured.

tools.returns: per analyzer (loudness, video, transcript, beats): { state: done | running | queued | failed | cancelled, ... }; loudness when done: { cached, hasAudio, seconds, integratedLufs, loudnessRangeLu, truePeakDbtp, silence: { thresholdDb, minSeconds, count, ranges: [{ start, end, startSeconds, endSeconds }] } }; video when done: { cached, hasVideo, seconds, sourceFps, cleanScore, stability, sharpness, exposure, frozen, measures: { shakePercent, panPerSecond, blur, brightness }, best: { start, end, startSeconds, endSeconds, cleanScore, ... }, shots, cuts: { threshold, count, list: [{ frame, seconds, score }] }, frozen: [{ start, end, startSeconds, endSeconds }], drops: [{ frame, seconds, missingSeconds }], stretches: [{ start, end, quality: good | fair | poor, cleanScore }], perSecond: { firstSecond, cleanScore: [], stability: [], sharpness: [], exposure: [], panPerSecond: [] } } (frames are project frames of the media); transcript when done: { cached, hasAudio, seconds, language, model, words, segments, fillers: { hesitation, maybe }, pauses, pauseSeconds, opening }; beats when done: { cached, hasAudio, seconds, bpm (null: no steady beat), confidence, beatCount, beatFrames, firstBeat: { frame, seconds }, lastBeat, beats: { frames: [], seconds: [], range?, count?, truncated? }, onsetCount, onsets?: { count, list: [{ frame, seconds, strength }] } (with range) }

tools.name: media_rank
tools.description: Rank video takes by how clean they are: cleanScore 0-1 from stability (no camera shake beyond smooth pans), sharpness (in focus) and exposure, with frozen stretches counted against it. Each take has its components and its best stretch (the cleanest window seconds inside one shot, in project frames usable as in). Runs or joins the video analysis (cached) and waits up to a minute; takes still being analysed come back under pending: call again.

media.description: Media ids from project_read. Default: the media imported from folder, or all the project's video.

folder.description: An absolute folder path: rank the project's media whose files are in it (import them first with media_import). Not together with media.

by.description: What to rank by: clean (default, the whole take's cleanScore), best (its best stretch's cleanScore), or one component.

window.description: Length of the best stretch in seconds (default 5).

tools.returns: { by, ranked: [{ rank, media, name, cached, seconds, cleanScore, stability, sharpness, exposure, frozen, measures: { shakePercent, panPerSecond, blur, brightness }, shots, drops, best: { start, end, startSeconds, endSeconds, cleanScore, stability, sharpness, exposure, frozen } }], pending?: [{ media, state, progress }], failed?, skipped?, note }

tools.name: transcript_read
tools.description: What's said in a media file, transcribed on this Mac with whisper.cpp (language detected; pass language to force one): text lines with word indices and frames, or each word with its frames; fillers and pauses (at least 0.3 s, aligned to the silences when the loudness analysis is cached) are marked and listed. Pass media, or item (any clip or sound on any track: its speech is read, a take's microphone for its camera or screen). Paged: pass from = next.from for more. The first call transcribes (the very first downloads the speech model) and waits up to a minute; if it answers running, call again. Cached after.

media.description: A media id from project_read (or pass item).

item.description: An item id on any track instead of media: the transcript of the file its speech is (its own sound, or its take's microphone).

range.description: Only words overlapping these project frames of the media [start, end).

format.description: text (default): one line per sentence (per phrase on a long take), 'w<first word index> [start–end] words', {fillers} and (pause n s) inline. words: each word with start and end frames.

from.description: The first word index to list (next.from of the previous page).

language.description: The spoken language as a code (en, pl, ...), or auto (default: detect). A cached transcript in another language is redone.

tools.returns: { media, item?, state, cached, language, model, seconds, words (total), segments, shown: { from, to }, text (format text) | list: [{ i, text, start, end, unsure?, filler? }] (format words), fillers: [{ i, n, text, start, end, kind: hesitation | maybe }], pauses: [{ start, end, startSeconds, endSeconds, after, edge?, silent? }], phrases?: n (long take, see note), list phrases?: [{ from, to, start, end }] (format words), next?: { from } } or { transcript: { state: running | queued, progress, stage? } } (frames are project frames of the media)

tools.name: transcript_edit
tools.description: Cut by text: remove words (ranges of transcript_read's word ids), pauses (at least min seconds) and/or hesitation fillers (um, uh, yyy, eee; never the 'maybe' ones) of a media file from every main-track clip that uses it (or whose linked microphone does), as one edit on your turn (Undo turn reverts it). Respects each clip's in, length and speed; the main track closes up, items on other tracks don't move. With item it cuts that item and what belongs to it instead (docs_read footage). Cuts snap to frames and keep a couple of frames next to the words that stay; adjacent cuts merge; words no longer in the edit are skipped with a note. dryRun returns the plan. Makes the transcript if needed (if it answers running, call again).

media.description: A media id from project_read; may be left out when exactly one media with sound is on the main track, or when item is given.

item.description: Cut this item (any track) and what belongs to it instead of every main clip of the media; word ids are its speech's transcript_read ids (transcript_read with the same item).

remove.description: Word ranges to cut, both ends included, e.g. [{"from": "w12", "to": "w20"}, {"from": "w31"}].

min.description: Pauses at least this many seconds long (default 0.5). A little quiet stays next to each word.

fillers.description: true: also cut the hesitation fillers (English and Polish).

dryRun.description: true: only say what would be cut and the new length.

tools.returns: { media, item?, applied, removed: [{ words?, text, pauses?, fillers?, mediaFrames: { start, end }, frames, seconds, clips }], framesRemoved, secondsSaved, revision, duration, seconds, durationBefore, notes? } (frames: the edit's, mediaFrames: project frames of the media)

tools.name: captions_make
tools.description: Captions from a media file's transcript: a captions item on its own text track that follows the main-track clips using the media (or their linked microphone; item: any clip or sound, docs_read footage): later cuts, trims and transcript_edit removals keep it in sync. Cards are 1-2 lines, broken at pauses and sentence ends. mode line shows a card at a time, word also accents the speaking word (karaoke), single shows one word at a time. If the media already has captions they're remade from the transcript (corrections kept when the words are the same). If it answers running, call again. Fix words, force card starts or change settings afterwards with timeline_edit's edit_captions op; restyle with update_item style (as on text).

media.description: A media id from project_read; may be left out when exactly one media with sound is on the main track, or when item is given.

item.description: An item id on any track instead of media: captions of its speech (its own sound, or its take's microphone).

mode.description: line (default): a card at a time; word: the card with the speaking word accented; single: one word at a time.

look.description: A text-style module id (default text.caption: white lines on dark boxes near the bottom). modules_list kind text-style lists them.

lines.description: How words are grouped (defaults: maxChars what fits the canvas at the look's size, at most 32; maxLines 2, maxSeconds 3, pause 0.3).

hideFillers.description: Leave hesitations (um, uh, yyy) out of the captions.

tools.returns: { media, item, remade, mode, words, cards: [{ from, to, words: 'w12–w18', text }] (the first 40; frames of the edit), cardCount, revision, notes? }

tools.name: subtitles_export
tools.description: Subtitles as a file: the cards every captions item draws (corrections applied, hidden words and fillers left out, word and single modes as whole cards) and the text items of "Subtitles" tracks (an imported .srt / .vtt), merged by time, at the edit's times after cuts. Writes .srt or .vtt; no video is rendered. Refused when there are no captions or subtitles, or when the file exists (pass overwrite).

format.description: srt (default) or vtt; taken from path's extension when it has one.

path.description: An absolute path inside the project folder, ending in .srt or .vtt (default: next to project.json, named after the project). Paths outside it are refused: the user saves elsewhere from the Export dialog.

overwrite.description: Replace a file already there (never a subtitles file the project imported).

tools.returns: { path, format, cues, first: [{ from, to, time, text }] (the first 5; frames of the edit), note }

tools.name: export_video
tools.description: Export the .mp4, only when the user asks: the Export dialog's job (they see progress, can cancel). Waits until saved; one at a time; a taken name gets " 2". Asks on a card unless Auto and the user named the folder in this message.

folder.description: Desktop, Movies, Downloads, Documents or a path; default the dialog's

range.description: all (default), In to Out, or the selected clips

tools.returns: { saved, seconds, size, picture, preset, tookSeconds, warnings? }

tools.name: media_import
tools.description: Add footage, music or images from disk to the project's media. Pass path or paths: a file, a folder (the media files directly inside it, not subfolders), or a list of paths. Files are referenced where they are, never changed; one inside another Uncut project (media_search) is copied into media/imports. At most 50 files per call. Returns each new media entry with its length, size, fps and sound, plus what was skipped or failed and why. Undo turn removes what it imported.

path.description: An absolute path (or ~/...) to a file or a folder.

name.description: A display name, for a single file only.

tools.returns: revision, imported: [{ id, kind, name, path, frames, seconds, fps, width, height, hasAudio }], skipped: [{ path, reason }], failed: [{ path, message }]

tools.name: media_download
tools.description: Download a picture, video or sound from the web (a logo, a screenshot, a demo video found with WebSearch or WebFetch) into the project's media/downloads folder and import it into Media. Public https only; image, video and audio files up to 300 MB. Pass the file's own address, not the page it's on. Undo turn removes the import (the file stays in media/downloads). A font file (WOFF2, WOFF, TTF, OTF) goes to the project's fonts folder instead, named after its family (docs_read graphics).

name.description: A display name for the media (e.g. "Argent logo"); the file is named from it too. For a font file: its family ("Geist").

tools.returns: revision, imported: [{ id, kind, name, path, frames, seconds, fps, width, height, hasAudio }], source: { url, bytes, type }; for a font file: font: { family, file, url, bytes }, note

tools.name: generate_media
tools.description: Make an image, video or sound with a generator into Media › Generated, with its prompt, as an edit of this turn. generate.svg is free: pass the SVG or HTML you wrote as content (kind image: a still; kind video: an animation up to 12 s). generate.gpt-image, generate.veo, generate.sound and plugins' generators (modules_list kind generator) bill the user's own API key; without it the result says which key is needed. Over $1 asks the user on a card.

prompt.description: What to make, in words (stored with the media). For generate.svg, what the content shows.

kind.description: Default: the generator's own (gpt-image image, veo video, sound audio, svg image).

size.description: gpt-image: 1536x1024, 1024x1024 or 1024x1536. veo: 16:9 or 9:16. svg: canvas (default) or WIDTHxHEIGHT.

seconds.description: veo: 4, 6 or 8. sound: 0.5 to 30 (default 5). svg video: up to 12 (default 5). music: 30 to 180.

options.description: A plugin's generator: option values by id, e.g. {"voice": "George"}.

name.description: The file's name (without extension); default from the prompt.

content.description: generate.svg only: the SVG document or HTML page you wrote (no network, images as data: URLs, system fonts).

tools.returns: id, kind, name, path, frames, seconds, width, height, hasAudio, revision, model, estimatedCost (US dollars), turnSpend; or needsKey / approved: false with what to tell the user

tools.name: modules_list
tools.description: Installed modules (transitions, text styles, components, effects, audio processors…). Without arguments: every module's id and purpose by kind, and the plugins. kind: that kind's modules whole, with their params schema (components also their placement: default size, devices' screens; text styles their look; transitions their frame limits); showsInPreview says whether the preview draws (or plays) a module as the export does. ids: just those modules, whole.
tools.returns: without arguments { modules: { <kind>: { <id>: purpose } }, plugins?, next }; with kind or ids the modules' manifests (params, placement, look, limits, showsInPreview)

tools.name: graphic_write
tools.description: Write a graphic's HTML into graphics/, for what components can't do. The HTML defines render(t, info), called every frame with t = seconds from the item's start and info {frame, fps, duration, width, height, props}; it draws into a transparent canvas-size page. render must finish within 5 s a frame. No network; fonts and the project's media (uncut.frame, uncut:media/<id>): docs_read graphics. Files are never overwritten: to change a graphic, write a new name, or pass from (its file) and edits [{old, new}] instead of html for a new revision (<file>-2.html, …). Then insert {"type":"graphic","src":"graphics/<name>"} on a video track with timeline_edit. A graphic for the whole film is ONE item spanning it, never several items of one file.

name.description: The file name, e.g. counter.html (it becomes graphics/counter.html). Required with html; with from, optional (default: the next free <file>-<n>.html).

html.description: The document's body: markup, <style> and a <script> defining render(t, info).

from.description: Edit mode: an existing graphic's file name (film.html or graphics/film.html) to start from instead of html.

edits.description: Edit mode: replacements applied in order to from's HTML; each old is copied exactly from the file and must occur exactly once (else nothing is written).

tools.returns: the src to put on the item, or why it was refused

tools.name: shader_write
tools.description: A GPU shader effect for clips, saved in shaders/, for a look no effect gives (modules_list kind "effect" lists them). A TypeGPU function: typed params with ranges and the WGSL body of (uv, t, size, p) -> vec4f per pixel: uv 0-1 from top-left, t seconds from the clip's start (the only clock), size in px, p the params; frame(uv) reads the clip. Return the colour (alpha ignored). Limits (no while, bounded for, no storage or pointers, 16 KB): docs_read picture. Uncut checks, compiles and draws it on a sample (shown in the answer), then saves it as project.<name>, replacing one of that name. Apply it with timeline_edit: {"module":"effect.shader","params":{"shader":"project.<name>","values":{...}}} in the clip's effects.

name.description: The effect's name, e.g. heat-haze: its id becomes project.heat-haze.

title.description: What the Effects tab calls it (default from the name).

params.description: Its params, in the order p's fields have them: numbers (min, max, default) and switches are f32 (a switch is 0.0 or 1.0), colours vec3f (0-1, default "#rrggbb").

body.description: The function's arguments and block in WGSL, e.g. (uv, t, size, p) { let c = frame(uv + vec2f(sin(uv.y * 40.0 + t * 4.0) * p.amount, 0.0)); return vec4f(c.rgb, 1.0); } (leave p out when there are no params).

tools.returns: its id and a picture of it on a sample frame, or why it was refused

tools.name: ui_show
tools.description: Point the user at something in the editor: a frame and/or an item becomes a pill over the preview ("Agent changed 0:12–0:18") the user clicks to jump there and select it; it never moves their playhead or selection. panel opens a panel. Use it to show a result, e.g. the cut you made with that clip.

select.description: The id of one timeline item (the editor selects one item at a time).

panel.description: Left: media, text, elements (backgrounds and components), audio. Right: inspector, agent (this chat), checks (the taste checks list).

tools.returns: what was shown

tools.name: project_check
tools.description: Taste checks on the current project (text timing and size, typefaces, the frame's edges, blank stretches, transitions, music and sound; docs_read production lists every rule). Each finding has the rule id, severity (warn or info), one sentence, the item ids, the frame (and range) to look at, and either fix (ops you can send as they are with timeline_edit, with a summary) or a hint. Checks never block the export; rules the project turned off (checks.disabled) are left out.

severity.description: Only warnings, or only info notes.

tools.returns: { revision, warnings, notes, checks: [{ rule, severity, message, items, frame, seconds, range, fix | hint }], disabled }

tools.name: measure
tools.description: sound: the exported mix by role, each effect against the voice with a verdict and gain change; level sound by it. colour: luma, black/white points, RGB, saturation, cast and the temperature and tint that remove it, for frames or clips (2+: a match). temperature + warmer, tint + magenta.
tools.returns: sound: { levels, master, roles, music, effects: [{ item, label, kind, at, peak, against, under, verdict }], overTime }; colour: { directions, frames | items: [{ frame | item, luma, blackPoint, whitePoint, meanRgb, saturationPercent, whiteBalance, neutralise }], match }

tools.name: library_search
tools.description: Search the sound library: royalty-free music or sound effects online (Openverse without a key, Freesound when the user stored that key), CC0 and CC BY only (CC BY needs credit, project_read lists it), or with source "included": for sfx Uncut's bundled CC0 sound effects (designed and meme sounds) plus matching files from the user's own sound folders (`yours`, ids folder:…); for music the user's own sound folders and Music library (`yours`; Uncut ships no music, so look there first). Search by sound, meme name, or a genre or mood for music: docs_read sound has the search words, meme clips and Openverse's limits.

query.description: What to search for. Required unless source is included.

source.description: Default openverse. included: the bundled sound effects (sfx) or the user's own music (music).

license.description: cc0: only sounds that need no credit.

length.description: short < 30 s, medium 30 s to 2 min, long > 2 min.

category.description: source included: whoosh, transition, swipe, ui, pop, impact, riser, notification, success, glitch, typing, crowd or meme.

tools.returns: { hits: [{ id, title, creator, frames, license, tags }] (the best 8), total, page, pages, more?, searched?, clip? } or, for included, { sounds (16 at most), more?, yours?, clip? } (sfx) or { yours, total, more? } (music)

tools.name: library_add
tools.description: Add a library_search result to the project's media: the file is downloaded (or a bundled sound or a file of the user's folders copied) into the project's media/ folder and added as audio media with its credits (source, creator, licence, attribution), as an edit on your turn. Returns the media id and length; then put it on an audio track with timeline_edit. A sound already in the project returns its media id.

id.description: A hit id from library_search, e.g. openverse:eab8a6e2-0ac8-4615-9e0d-ebde30523783, freesound:351256, sfx:dramatic-boom or folder:<id> (the user's own file).

tools.returns: { media, path, frames, seconds, license, revision }

tools.name: screen_record
tools.description: Record the user's screen or a window (a browser window shows as its page title) on this Mac for some seconds, as media of this turn. The user is always asked first on a card in the Agent tab, where they pick the screen or window (yours preselected by name) and can say no; nothing is ever recorded without their Record. The result gives the media id and the source's name, or that the user said no.

source.description: The screen or window to suggest, by (part of) its name, e.g. "Chrome" or "Screen 1". The user can pick another.

seconds.description: How long to record, after a 3-2-1 countdown.

tools.returns: id, name, path, frames, seconds, width, height, source, revision; or approved: false with what to tell the user

tools.name: argent_boot
tools.description: Boot an iOS simulator or Android emulator with Argent so you can record the app. Without device it lists the bootable ones by name (and the running ones). With a device (an id or a name from that list) the user is asked on a card in the Agent tab first: nothing boots without their Boot. A device the user allowed once in this chat boots again without asking. Not in Look only. After it boots, record with argent_record {device, bundleId (the app to open), flow or seconds}.

device.description: A bootable device's id or name; leave it out to list them.

bundleId.description: The app you will open and record after it boots (shown on the card).

tools.returns: bootable and running devices; or booted: true with the device id to record; or approved: false with what to do instead

tools.name: media_search
tools.description: Search the user's media from their other projects on this Mac: captures (simulator and screen recordings), imports and generations, newest first, each with its path, kind, length, project, device or app and when it was made. Bring one in with media_import {path} (a file inside another project is copied into this one's media/imports; others are referenced). Search here before drawing a placeholder for product footage.

query.description: Words to match in the name, file, project, device or app, e.g. "argent demo"; empty lists the newest.

kind.description: Only this kind of media or this origin.

tools.returns: found: [{ path, name, kind, origin, seconds, size, project, device, app, created, import }]

tools.name: ask_user
tools.description: Ask the user a question on a card in the Agent tab and wait for the answer (up to 15 minutes): options to pick (one, or several with multi) and/or their own words. Use it before building whenever something material is unclear or missing (the brand, the logo, the audience, the length, the format, the real assets) instead of guessing or inventing.

freeText.description: A box for their own answer (default true; always on without options).

tools.returns: the picked options and the text, or that it was skipped

tools.name: brief_write
tools.description: Save the production brief (brief.json in the project), shown to the user as a Brief card they can edit. Co-write it with the user before building a new video; write it again when it changes. It records the video's type (the critic's rubric and the sound limits follow it) and suggests the skills that fit: read them with skill_read.

assets.description: The real assets it uses (recordings, screenshots, the kit's logo).

type.description: The kind of video. The critic judges it as that kind (a tutorial needs no hook, a meme may be loud) and the sound limits follow it. Leave it out and Uncut guesses from the brief's words.

skills.description: Skills (names from the system prompt's Skills list) that fit this video. Leave it out and Uncut suggests a set from the type and the brief. Read the ones that fit with skill_read.

tools.returns: saved, or what's missing

tools.name: storyboard_propose
tools.description: Propose the storyboard / shot list for the user to approve on a card before you build (it waits up to 15 minutes). Each beat: start and end in seconds, entry and exit states, purpose, real assets, the sound it lands on, and optionally a still shown with it (up to 4; docs_read production). Propose last: the stills are what the user approves. While it waits, edits are refused (unanswered: all turn, so end it). The answer is approved (maybe with edited beats; keep what the stills show), or a change to make (propose again).

approve.description: Only when the user said nobody can answer ("decide yourself"): approve it yourself instead of waiting; the card says so. The critic loop still runs.

start.description: Seconds from the start of the video.

entry.description: What's on screen as the beat starts.

exit.description: What's on screen as it ends (the next beat's entry).

purpose.description: Why the beat is there: what the viewer gets from it.

assets.description: The real assets it shows (media names, kit logo, recordings).

sound.description: The beat, downbeat or hit it lands on.

still.description: A timeline frame (an integer from 0), or {"graphic": "film.html", "t": 12.5} (seconds) drawn alone without placing it.

tools.returns: approved with the beats to build, or the change asked for

tools.name: review_submit
tools.description: Ask Uncut's critic for a review round of the built video: a separate Claude that sees only frames Uncut renders now, the brief, the brand kit, the storyboard and a rubric for the brief's type and the active skills; it scores what applies and lists blockers (any one fails the round); docs_read production has the rest. Needs a contact_sheet of the edit and render_frames with phone true in this turn since the last round. From round 2, claim each fix by the last review's id; a claimed fix needs its moment rendered (render_frames) after your last change, and the critic checks it on fresh frames. You don't score it yourself.

fixes.description: What you fixed since the last round, by the review's ids.

defect.description: A blocker or defect id from the last review (d1, d2, …).

scores.description: Ignored: Uncut's critic scores the video, not you.

defects.description: Ignored: the critic lists the defects.

notes.description: Ignored by the critic (it never sees your reasoning).

tools.returns: the critic's round: scores with evidence, blockers and defects with ids, each claimed fix verified or not, the determinism check and what to do next

tools.name: docs_read
tools.description: Uncut's reference for one area: how its items and fields fit together, with exact JSON examples and limits. edits: every timeline_edit op; production: the steps for a new video (brand, brief, storyboard, build, sound, critic, checks), skills, styles; text; picture (also effects, shaders); sound (also music, the sound library); components; graphics (graphic_write, libraries, fonts, generate_media); footage (import, transcripts, captions, subtitles, recording). Read a topic before you first work in that area in a conversation.
tools.returns: the topic's reference text

tools.name: plan_read
tools.description: The project's plan as it is now: the brief, the storyboard with its beats, and the last review with its defect ids (the ids review_submit's fixes name). A message's <plan> says "Unchanged" when it hasn't changed; read it here when you no longer have it.
tools.returns: the <plan> block, or that nothing is planned

tools.name: skill_read
tools.description: Read an installed skill's instructions: a recipe from a plugin (Uncut's own: launch promo, product demo, motion craft, sound design, brand application, make a brand kit and more). The system prompt's Skills list has every skill by name and when it fits; read one before you start a task it fits, then follow every rule in it. The project then uses it: the critic checks its review checklist.

name.description: The skill's name, as in the Skills list (launch-promo, sound-design, …).

tools.name: brand_read
tools.description: Read the project's brand kit (colours with roles, fonts with their files, logos, tone, taglines, URLs, do's and don'ts, style guide) and skills, with each logo as an image (an SVG drawn as a PNG for you; graphics keep it vector), or one of the kit's files: a logo or example frame comes back as an image with its path for media_import. Without an active kit it lists the user's kits.

kit.description: A kit id (default: the project's kit).

file.description: A file of the kit, e.g. its logos.light name.

tools.returns: the kit and skills, or the file

tools.name: brand_write
tools.description: Write into a brand kit (a field you pass replaces that field): colours, fonts (with their font files), logos, tone and the rest. Changing an existing kit's colours or fonts needs the user's OK on a before and after card. A style from a reference goes in style (its own guide attached to the kit), never in colors or fonts. A new name and no kit makes a new kit (scope says where), the project's kit if it has none. Logos and font files: a path, a folder or an https address; SVG stays vector. Only what the user gave or approved or the brand's own site shows, never invented brand facts.

scope.description: A new kit's home: global (default), the user's library; project, pinned to this project.

file.description: The font's file (.woff2, .woff, .ttf, .otf): a file of the kit, a path or an https address. Graphics, texts and components then load it.

logos.description: Logo files by slot: light (on light backgrounds), dark (on dark), mark (the icon). Each: a file of the kit, a path, or an https address (SVG, PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF).

import.description: A file, a folder or an https address to bring logos and font files from: logos fill the empty slots by their names (mark, icon: mark; dark, white: dark; else light), font files are added to fonts.

tools.returns: the kit as saved

tools.name: reference_frames
tools.description: A contact sheet of a reference video or image file on disk that isn't in the project (it isn't imported): frames spread over its length, for reading a style (palette, type, shot lengths, transitions, camera, grain) without copying its content.

path.description: The file's absolute path (~/ and $HOME/ work).

tools.returns: the sheet with each cell's time, the file's length and size

tools.name: beat_grid
tools.description: The beat grid of the music on the timeline in timeline frames: tempo, beats, downbeats (bar starts, the strongest beat of each 4), the strongest hits and the drop (the downbeat where the music gets much busier, or null), from the beats analysis; with snap, each frame you give with the nearest beat and downbeat, to put cuts and state changes on the beat and big moments on a downbeat.

item.description: An audio item (default: the longest music on the timeline).

tools.returns: tempo, beats, downbeats and hits in timeline frames, and the snaps

insertText.description: Text in a look (a text-style module), as one op: the item gets the look's size, weight, position and in/out moves (the rest of the look, e.g. its outline, shadow or box, applies while the item doesn't set those fields), plus the looks it comes with (a kicker above a title) on their own text tracks; it goes on the top-most text track free for [start, start + duration), else a new one on top.

look.description: A text-style module id, e.g. text.big-title, text.caption, text.boxed-label (modules_list kind text-style lists them with their looks).

text.description: Markup: **bold**, [[accent]], `mono`, \n for a line break. Default: the look's placeholder.

id.description: The new item's id (default: the look's name, numbered).

style.description: Style fields over the look's, canvas px: size, weight, font, color, align, tracking, lineHeight, uppercase, stroke {width, color}, shadow {x, y, blur, color, opacity}, background {color, opacity, padding, radius, wrap box|lines}; false for stroke, shadow or background removes the look's.

transform.description: The text box's top-left and width in canvas px, over the look's.

animation.description: In/out moves instead of the look's (frames), or null for none.

alone.description: Leave out the looks it comes with.

putOnMain.description: Put on Main: a picture off the main track (a clip, component, graphic or text) goes into it at the cut nearest frame (default: where it is), and what comes after ripples. A take's parts (its group: microphone, Mac sound, the other picture) over exactly its stretch become linked to it (linkedTo, their own in points kept) and stay on their tracks under it, following it from then on; a sound of a take puts the take's picture (the screen, else the camera) on Main. The track it leaves empty goes.

item.description: The picture's id, or one of its take's sounds.

frame.description: Where it should land (timeline frame of its start); it goes in at the main-track cut nearest its middle.

detachAudio.description: Detach audio: the clip's sound becomes an audio item (same media, in point, speed and start; the clip's volume, fades and volume keys move to it) on the first audio track free for that stretch (or a new one, or `track`), and the clip gets mute: true. Captions and transcript cuts keep following the clip on main.

id.description: The new audio item's id (default audio-N).

track.description: An audio track that is free there (default: picked or made).

setSpeed.description: Change the speed of a clip or an audio item: 0.1 to 10 (2 = twice as fast). It keeps playing the same stretch of its media, so its duration becomes duration x old speed / new speed (main clips after it ripple; on a free track the next item must leave room). keepPitch false lets the pitch follow the speed (like tape); true keeps it (the default).

replaceRange.description: Replace a fragment without moving anything (an overwrite edit): timeline frames [from, to) of a clip or audio item play another media from its frame in (default 0) at normal speed. The item is split at both ends and the piece keeps its box, effects and volume; it stays exactly as long, so nothing after it shifts and the cut stays in sync with the music.

editCaptions.description: Change a captions item as one op: fix words (by transcript_read's word id; "" hides a word, null goes back to the transcript's), force a new card at a word (or stop forcing one), switch the mode, change the grouping or hide fillers. It becomes one update_item.

on.description: true (default): a card starts at this word; false: no forced start.

lines.description: Grouping settings over the item's (null for a field: its default): maxChars, maxLines (1 or 2), maxSeconds, maxWords, pause.

cover.description: true: stretch the captions over the whole main track again (after clips were added past them).

insertDeviceFrame.description: A device frame (component.device-frame) with footage under it, as one op: the footage is a clip on a free video track above main (else a new one), its box the frame's screen (cover, the screen's rounded corners); the frame goes on the video track above it; both from start for duration. Default box: centred, 86% of the canvas height (a browser 80% of its width).

media.description: Video or image media for the screen; leave it out for the frame alone.

in.description: Where the clip starts in its media (project frames).

box.description: The frame's box in canvas pixels: x, y (its top-left) and h (the width follows the device's shape).

color.description: The frame's colour (a theme token or CSS colour).

url.description: browser: the address in its bar.

hold.description: Footage shorter than the frame holds its last frame (a freeze) instead of looping.

placeItem.description: Place an item without fighting overlaps. On a free track: at start when that stretch is free; otherwise place "after" puts it at the first free frame after what is in the way, "free-track" keeps the start on another track of the same kind that is free there (a new track next to it when none is), "ripple" moves the track's items from start on later by what is needed. On the main track it goes in at index (or the cut at start) and the rest ripples.

track.description: The track to put it on (for a move, default: its own).

item.description: A new item ({id, type, duration, …} as insert_item takes) or the id of an item to move.

start.description: The frame it should start at (free tracks).

setTransitionTrim.description: set_transition that may trim the clips at the cut: an overlapping transition needs spare media on both sides (half its length); allowTrim: true trims exactly what is missing off the incoming clip's start and the outgoing clip's end before it is set.
